name_note: The GTDB species s__Escherichia coli is broader than the NCBI species: it also contains genomes that NCBI labels Shigella sonnei and Shigella flexneri.

sentences.text: Escherichia coli is described as the most predominant facultative anaerobic commensal bacterium of the vertebrate intestinal microbiota.
A review states that E. coli accompanies humans from birth as a commensal of the gut microbiota, while some strains cause intestinal and extraintestinal diseases.
The same review calls it the best-studied single-celled organism in the world and a model organism for the molecular mechanisms of key life processes.
A narrative review reports that particular pathotypes, among them adherent-invasive and diffusely adherent E. coli, contribute to the development and progression of inflammatory bowel disease.
In a Southeast Asian cohort, intestinal carriage of E. coli sequence-type 131 was associated with compositional shifts in the faecal microbiome without a reduction in species alpha-diversity.
